title: Embeddings are a Lookup Table
tagline: An embedding layer is just indexing a learned table of vectors — one row per token
summary: A 10-token, 2-dimensional embedding matrix drawn two ways at once: a heat-map table you index into and a scatter map you can drag. Click a token to light up its row and read off e = E[i]; nudge the two coordinates with sliders or drag the point across the plane and watch the row and its position move as one. Vowels and consonants start pre-clustered, so you can feel the punchline directly — similarity between tokens is nothing but distance between rows, and training is just moving those rows.
highlights: See an embedding matrix E rendered simultaneously as a heat-map table and a 2-D scatter of points — the same array, two views.
Click any token id to light up its row and read the lookup e = E[i] as a dense vector.
Drag a point across the plane (or nudge its two sliders) and watch the corresponding row recolor in lock-step.
Vowels and consonants begin pre-clustered, so dragging one across the border flips its nearest neighbour and makes 'similarity = nearby rows' tangible.
Sets up the companion char-MLP explainer: a training step edits only the rows of the tokens it actually used.
